title: World Bank Deepens Commitment to Building Human Capital and Inclusive Development in the Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: The World Bank approved a 2022-2026 partnership framework for the DRC that put strong emphasis on human development, improved basic services, governance, and stabilization.
source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank press release with explicit country-program priorities and date.
period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period policy and baseline context.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: it reflects the incumbent government's strategic priorities, but not a personally authored social policy outcome.
contrary_evidence: The same release says poverty is rising and governance remains weak.

title: The World Bank Supports Free Primary Education and Maternal and Child Health Improvements in the DRC
claim: The World Bank said the education project would help roll out free primary education, support more than nine million children to re-enroll and stay in school, and expand access for poor children excluded from schooling.
source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank release with concrete program design and expected reach.
period_fit: Pre-2022 baseline that remained relevant in 2022.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the project supports Tshisekedi-era policy, but delivery depended on implementers and schools.
contrary_evidence: The same release implies many children were still excluded and schools were reopening from lockdown.

title: Child survival
claim: UNICEF said many DRC children still die before age five from preventable diseases and that health delivery is hindered by stock-outs, underpaid staff, poor quality care, and limited financial access.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country program page with explicit service-delivery diagnosis.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is national service delivery under the incumbent government, but not uniquely ruler-caused.
contrary_evidence: The same page also says UNICEF is working with partners to vaccinate children and reduce child mortality.

title: Emergency response
claim: UNICEF said that in 2022 the DRC faced two Ebola epidemics and that more than 1.3 million under-5 children needed treatment for severe wasting, 6.6 million children needed emergency water and sanitation, and 2.7 million children needed emergency education support.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF country page with a quantified humanitarian needs estimate.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: these needs are partly structural and conflict-driven, but they frame incumbent responsibility for response.
contrary_evidence: The same page also describes UNICEF’s ongoing response efforts.

title: Safe water for students and families in Walungu
claim: UNICEF reported that it had connected a South Kivu primary school to safe drinking water and installed hygienic toilets, improving hygiene and school conditions.
source_confidence_reason: Direct field story with concrete service-delivery details and date.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: a UNICEF-supported local service intervention, not a uniquely presidential act.
contrary_evidence: The story implies the school previously lacked water and children had to fetch it elsewhere.

title: Improving girls’ access to education in Kasai
claim: UNICEF said that in Kasai only 12 girls out of 100 boys attend lower secondary school and that it was running a girls-education pilot with new classrooms, sanitation, and boreholes.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF field report with explicit gender-gap and intervention details.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the project addresses a government-relevant gap, but delivery is mainly partner-led.
contrary_evidence: The same story shows a severe preexisting gender gap and early marriage pressures.

title: Education Cannot Wait and UNICEF with partners call for substantial increase in funding for crisis-affected children in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: UNICEF said 3.2 million children aged 6 to 11 were out of school, rural completion was far below urban completion, and only 38 percent of primary schools had access to water.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF/ECW press release with quantified access and equity gaps.
period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period evidence, even though some figures use earlier survey data.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a 2022 state-of-service baseline under the incumbent government, but not a pure ruler-attributable outcome.
contrary_evidence: The same release also describes a funded resilience programme and government collaboration.

title: The dilemma of schools that shelter DRC’s displaced families
claim: UNICEF said more than 2,000 schools had closed since January 2022 because of insecurity and displacement, depriving children of education.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF field story with a clear quantified disruption and date.
period_fit: Directly spans the 2022 target year and its consequences.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the closures are driven by conflict and displacement, but the national government bears response responsibility.
contrary_evidence: The same story shows UNICEF and partners building temporary learning spaces where possible.

title: The impact of the cash transfer intervention in the commune of Nsele in Kinshasa
claim: UNICEF said the cash-transfer intervention reached about 23,000 households initially and then about 16,000 of the most vulnerable households in the social-protection phase, with complementary training on women’s leadership, rights, and financial management.
source_confidence_reason: Impact report with concrete target population and programme content.
period_fit: Retrospective evidence about a programme active in the target period.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the programme was delivered with government-facing targeting lessons, but implementation was partner-led.
contrary_evidence: The same report later says the evaluation found only limited impacts on food security and dietary diversity.

title: The impact of the cash transfer intervention in the commune of Nsele in Kinshasa
claim: UNICEF reported that the quantitative evaluation found limited impacts on household food security, resilience coping, and dietary diversity, and that implementation problems needed correction before scaling up.
source_confidence_reason: Impact evaluation with explicit negative findings and implementation diagnosis.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is about a government-supported social protection effort, but the weakness is mainly implementation-level.
contrary_evidence: The qualitative interviews were more positive and the report notes lessons for future targeting.

title: Lancement de la 3eme phase du projet conjoint de transferts monétaires humanitaires aux populations vulnérables à Kinshasa
claim: UNICEF said the third phase of the Kinshasa cash-transfer project targeted nearly 4,000 vulnerable households, including pregnant women, children under five, disabled heads of household, and elderly people.
source_confidence_reason: Direct program announcement with clear vulnerable-group targeting.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: government collaboration is explicit, but implementation is partner-led.
contrary_evidence: The note also says the programme was a continuation of earlier COVID-related response phases.

title: Children’s education, a priority for Marlène
claim: UNICEF said more than 4,000 vulnerable families in N’Sele received unconditional cash transfers that helped them care for families and educate children while improving access to basic social services.
source_confidence_reason: Direct beneficiary story with quantified reach and concrete uses of assistance.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the benefit is real but delivered through a donor-supported programme, not a uniquely presidential policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The story is anecdotal and does not establish national-scale effects.

title: UNICEF and partners respond to unprecedented cholera outbreak in Sankuru, DR Congo
claim: UNICEF said more than 30,000 people, including more than 17,000 children, were threatened by a cholera outbreak in Sankuru and that 24 people had died, including 8 children.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF emergency release with specific caseload and mortality figures.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: outbreak response reflects state capacity, though the event itself is not ruler-caused.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF says health, water and sanitation services were being deployed to respond.

title: Working with communities to curb cholera in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: WHO said that by late 2022 the DRC had reported more than 12,300 suspected cholera cases and 222 deaths in 17 provinces.
source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO regional office publication with a quantified national outbreak snapshot.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a national public-health crisis under the incumbent government.
contrary_evidence: WHO frames this as an outbreak control effort and discusses community response.

title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo declares Ebola resurgence in North Kivu
claim: WHO reported the 2022 Ebola resurgence in North Kivu and said a prior flare-up had been brought under control in about two months with 11 cases and 6 deaths.
source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO outbreak report with dates and case/death counts.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: outbreak control was a state responsibility under Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: WHO emphasizes vaccination and surveillance as the response mechanism.

title: WHO Global Health Emergency Appeal: DRC
claim: WHO said that during vaccine responses in the DRC, 2,635,401 people were vaccinated against cholera, 162,518 against meningitis, and 1,180,268 children against measles.
source_confidence_reason: Primary WHO publication with explicit vaccination delivery figures.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: these are government-implemented public-health responses supported by WHO.
contrary_evidence: The appeal also says the country remains in a high-grade emergency with many outbreaks.

title: UNHCR deeply concerned by renewed violence displacing thousands in North Kivu, DR Congo
claim: UNHCR said more than 72,000 people had been displaced by fighting in North Kivu and that displaced families were struggling to access food and clean water.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNHCR briefing note with displacement and welfare consequences.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: displacement is driven by conflict, but response and protection are national-government responsibilities.
contrary_evidence: UNHCR notes some emergency assistance and use of temporary shelters.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo Country Strategic Plan (2021–2026)
claim: WFP said food and nutrition security in the DRC is hit by conflict, epidemics, climate events, weak infrastructure, and underinvestment in agriculture, health, and human capital.
source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP country strategy with a plain-language diagnosis of constraints.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a structural baseline, not purely ruler-caused, but it frames the incumbent's constraints.
contrary_evidence: The same plan says WFP supports government priorities rather than substituting for them.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Acute Food Insecurity Situation July - December 2022 and Projection for January - June 2023
publisher: IPC - Integrated Food Security Phase Classification
claim: IPC estimated that 26.4 million people in the DRC were facing acute food insecurity in mid- to late 2022, driven by poverty, conflict, displacement, low agricultural production, high food prices, and weak infrastructure.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IPC national analysis with quantified food insecurity and causal factors.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the causes are mixed, but the government is responsible for response and mitigation.
contrary_evidence: IPC also notes a slight improvement in the 2023 projection compared with late 2022.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo - Data in Emergencies (DIEM) Monitoring System – Household Survey – Round 4, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2022
claim: FAO said it ran a nationally representative 2022 household survey across 11 provinces to assess livelihoods, shocks, food security, consumption, and assistance needs.
source_confidence_reason: Primary FAO microdata catalogue entry with design and coverage details.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is measurement infrastructure rather than a ruler action, but it is strong evidence on the information environment.
contrary_evidence: The survey scope is only 11 of 26 provinces, so it is not a perfect national census.

title: Strengthening resilience in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic and contributing to poverty reduction in peri-urban Kinshasa through agricultural livelihoods support
claim: FAO reported that its Kinshasa COVID-response project aimed to strengthen the socioeconomic and nutritional situation of 2,550 affected households and to stabilize income, food access, and dietary diversification.
source_confidence_reason: FAO evaluation highlight with explicit target population, objectives, and delivery mechanisms.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the project was implemented with government collaboration, but it was not a purely presidential initiative.
contrary_evidence: FAO says COVID-19 had already reduced incomes and food security in low-income households.

title: Providing safety nets for the most vulnerable in the Democratic Republic of Congo: Incremental steps with a large footprint
claim: The STEP social-protection program benefited over 5.8 million people and supported 530,000 individuals with cash transfers, cash-for-work, investment grants, and training between 2014 and December 2022.
source_confidence_reason: World Bank results page with cumulative outcomes and dates through the target year.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the programme is government-linked but donor-implemented, so attribution is shared.
contrary_evidence: The same page makes clear this is an incremental safety-net effort rather than a comprehensive national system.

title: Empowering Girls and Enhancing Learning in the Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: The World Bank said the DRC had significant gender gaps in school attendance and learning outcomes, and that the resulting analysis helped design the Girls' Learning and Empowerment Project.
source_confidence_reason: World Bank results page with explicit link from evidence to policy design.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the Ministry of Finance and education authorities are involved, but this is still donor-led analysis.
contrary_evidence: The page shows the baseline problem was severe in 2017 and needed targeted intervention.

title: Spotlight on basic education completion and foundational learning: Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: UNESCO reported that basic education access expanded since 2016, but net enrolment was still only 69 percent, quality was weak because of underfunding and poor infrastructure, and 73 percent of Grade 6 students fell below minimum reading benchmarks.
source_confidence_reason: UNESCO knowledge-platform report summarizing a national education diagnosis with specific indicators.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a national education baseline rather than a pure ruler effect, but it frames feasible improvement.
contrary_evidence: The same report says access had expanded, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

title: Inclusive Governance Initiative Democratic Republic of the Congo Baseline Report
claim: UNDP said the project sought to make state entities more accountable to the whole population, including LGBTI people, and to support better laws, more responsive public services, and rights-affirming social norms.
source_confidence_reason: UNDP baseline report with clear human-rights and service-delivery objectives.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the report is about state accountability and inclusion, but it is a project baseline rather than an outcome evaluation.
contrary_evidence: The same report is only a baseline assessment, so it does not prove delivery.

title: Pauvreté et privations de l'enfant en 2021
claim: UNICEF's 2021 child-poverty study found that 74.6% of children aged 0-17 in the DRC were multidimensionally poor and faced overlapping privations in health, nutrition, education, protection, water, sanitation, and hygiene.
source_confidence_reason: Official UNICEF country report with explicit quantified baseline indicators and clear methodological framing.
period_fit: Baseline context immediately preceding the 2022 target year; useful for judging improvement against inherited deprivation.
ruler_attribution: Indirect baseline only; this measures inherited welfare conditions rather than Tshisekedi's own 2022 output.
contrary_evidence: The report is a 2021 baseline and does not itself measure 2022 change or ruler-specific delivery.

title: WHO Global Health Emergency Appeal: DRC
claim: WHO reported that during vaccine responses in the DRC, 2,635,401 people were vaccinated against cholera, 162,518 people were vaccinated against meningitis, and 1,180,268 children were vaccinated against measles.
source_confidence_reason: WHO publication with precise numerical response totals and direct country fit.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to the target year's health-crisis response capacity.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the vaccination output reflects a national response environment under the Tshisekedi administration, though implementation was carried by health authorities and partners.
contrary_evidence: The document is an appeal/summary of response activity, not a ruler-authored policy statement.

title: Ebola Virus Disease - Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: WHO said the North Kivu Ebola outbreak ended after no additional cases were found, and that 550 people in the affected health zone had been vaccinated using ring strategy, with frontline health workers forming most of the vaccinated group.
source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO outbreak bulletin with response metrics and a dated end-of-outbreak determination.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to crisis response in eastern DRC.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the response was led by the national health ministry with WHO and partners under the incumbent administration.
contrary_evidence: The bulletin credits the Ministry of Health and partners, so ruler-level attribution is indirect.

title: Ebola outbreak 2022 - Equateur Province, DRC
claim: WHO said the Equateur Ebola outbreak was brought to an end swiftly with limited transmission because of the robust response by national authorities.
source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO outbreak page with a clear conclusion on response effectiveness and timing.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is national-authority performance under Tshisekedi's government, not exclusive presidential causation.
contrary_evidence: The page is a public-health summary and does not isolate the president's own operational decisions.

title: Des solutions locales pour lutter contre la malnutrition
claim: In Tanganyika, UNICEF said 300 children suffering from severe malnutrition were being treated in Manono, and that cash transfers plus nutrition counseling helped a child named Mbuyu recover weight and improve diet within three months.
source_confidence_reason: Official UNICEF field story with concrete treatment and household-support details, though narrated through a beneficiary case.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to nutrition delivery under conflict and poverty constraints.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the intervention was UNICEF-supported and partnered with Germany, but it reflects the social-protection and health-delivery environment under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: This is a localized project story and does not prove national nutrition-system performance.

title: Building schools together with communities
claim: In Kasai-Central, UNICEF and villagers rebuilt Lunyenga Primary School in three months; the school was one of 22 built with community help, after more than 550 schools had been destroyed and over 100,000 students were left without classrooms.
source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 UNICEF account with specific reconstruction counts, timing, and student impact.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to education recovery from violence and displacement.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the rebuilding was done by UNICEF and communities, but it shows the administration's education-recovery environment and ability to enable local delivery.
contrary_evidence: The destruction was driven by prior conflict; the article does not isolate central-government funding as the sole driver of recovery.

title: Rendre l'eau disponible dans les centres de santé
claim: UNICEF said it installed a rainwater capture and storage system at the Sacre Coeur health centre in Walikale so the centre would have permanent water access, improve the quality of care, and protect patient dignity.
source_confidence_reason: Direct field report with concrete infrastructure and service-quality effects in a health facility.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to health-service delivery.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the project was UNICEF-supported with BMZ/KfW, but it evidences the wider public-service environment under the incumbent government.
contrary_evidence: This is a single facility intervention, not a systemwide health-sector audit.

title: Education Cannot Wait and UNICEF with partners call for substantial increase in funding for crisis-affected children in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: UNICEF said the DRC had about five million internally displaced persons, including 700,000 displaced in 2022 alone, and that 3.2 million children aged 6 to 11 were out of school; the joint programme in Tanganyika was presented as a model for girls' access and post-conflict recovery.
source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 UNICEF press release with clear casualty/displacement and schooling figures plus a government-linked programme example.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tightly relevant to crisis-linked education deprivation and response.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the figures largely reflect conflict and displacement pressures, but the programme operates in the national education environment under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The main causes are conflict and displacement, so this is partly a context source rather than a pure ruler-performance measure.

title: An integrated response for Central African refugee populations
claim: With ECHO support, UNICEF increased access to essential basic services that directly affect the survival of Central African refugees and host populations in northern DRC, including WASH and child- and gender-based-violence protection measures.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF story with explicit service-delivery claims, though much of the operational detail is narrative and donor-backed.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to vulnerable-group support and crisis service delivery.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: donor-backed local delivery is not solely presidential, but it reflects the national welfare environment and the government's ability to host and coordinate services.
contrary_evidence: The project is externally supported and does not demonstrate nationwide government delivery by itself.

title: Life is tough here
claim: UNICEF reported that a displaced mother in Rutshuru received emergency household items through a rapid-response distribution program, and that 4,700 other families received similar aid to improve hygiene and protect against diseases such as cholera.
source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 field story with named beneficiary and concrete assistance counts, though still a localized humanitarian vignette.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to displacement, hygiene, and emergency protection.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the aid is partner-delivered, but it reflects the government's inability or willingness to support displaced households in the existing crisis environment.
contrary_evidence: This is a localized emergency intervention, not a full measure of national social policy.
